content:
Hi,

I am Thomas from Berlin and experiment with a local AI ecosystem for studying (among other things) mathematics, including some first experiments with Lean. I am interested in learning how to combine Lean/Mathlib with local AI tools, and what workflows have proven useful in practice.

The idea: Strictly local AI as a "second desk lamp", inspired by the medieval term lucubrare ("to study by artificial light"), i.e. not attempting to replace mathematical work, but to support reading, exploration, note-taking, and occasionally formalization attempts.

For context, I have a short description of my first test projects here:
https://thothrde.github.io/local-ai-testprojects/index.html

Any comments or suggestions would be very welcome!

Hi Thomas, great to see this framing. I've been running a similar setup. cloud APIs rather than local models, but the same philosophy: AI as a research companion for formal mathematics, not a replacement for the work itself.

I've been using it specifically for Lean 4 / Mathlib proof development, building a library of zero-sorry formal proofs across dynamical systems. The workflow is iterative: spec the mathematical object precisely, run the proof loop, feed compiler errors back in. Closely mirrors what you're calling the Ralph Loop.

Results so far at github.com/velvetmonkey if you're curious. Always interested to compare notes on workflow, especially the Lean-specific parts.
